doc.title: Clark Terry interviewed by Joe Williams and Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, May 19, 1995

title: Williams joins Basie at the Manor House
summary: Williams recalls Basie recruiting him, calling him the top singer in the Midwest, and paying $25 then $50 a week.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Yeah, that was his favorite place man.

And I was in the room that he was in when I talked to him about joining the band. You know? That’s a story in itself, you see, me coming and joining him. I talked to him and he said, “why don’t you come with me and see what people all over the country think of your work?” He said, “you’re the top singer in the Midwest right now, in Cleveland, Detroit, Chicago, Milwaukee, and Minneapolis and Buffalo.” Even because I was working at the Moonglow for six weeks a year or something like that. He said “but” he said “in a little while, somebody’ll be saying, “hey, you hear Shorty over there singing? Shorty over there, the men’s room attendant,” he said, “you heard him sing? man oow wee.” He says, “somebody else is coming,” you know? He said, “why don’t you come with me and see what people all over the country think of your work?” And, “I can’t give you what you want or what you need, but I can give you something.” So you know what he gave me, $25 a week. But when I was working with you and him and the quintet, he would give me $50, which was something.
